articles.title: Novo eyes expansion in Central Asia
articles.summary: Danish pharmaceutical giant Novo (formerly Novo Nordisk) is eyeing Central Asia as a promising market for further expansion. The region currently accounts for less than 1% of revenue generated by Novo’s Middle East and Central Asia division, according to Burak Cem, the company’s regional vice president, who spoke to Kursiv.media on the sidelines of the ...
articles.body: Danish pharmaceutical giant Novo (formerly Novo Nordisk) is eyeing Central Asia as a promising market for further expansion. The region currently accounts for less than 1% of revenue generated by Novo’s Middle East and Central Asia division, according to Burak Cem , the company’s regional vice president, who spoke to Kursiv.media on the sidelines of the iCON obesity summit in Abu Dhabi. Novo, widely known for its diabetes medications, has been actively exploring obesity treatments in recent years. According to Cem, obesity is a far more complex condition than many people realize. Conventional advice to reduce calorie intake and increase physical activity does not work equally well for everyone. Obesity is, in fact, a chronic disease recognized by the World Health Organization, and its treatment requires a comprehensive approach that takes into account endocrine, psychological, hormonal and other factors. «One of the causes of diabetes is obesity,» Cem said, adding that the company has been investigating the mechanisms that regulate appetite and body weight. In particular, Novo has developed and manufactures Ozempic and Wegovy, medications that target glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptors. These drugs help activate the body’s natural appetite-regulating mechanisms and increase feelings of fullness, helping patients lose weight. Novo’s medications are already available in Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan, and the company intends to expand its presence in other Central Asian and CIS countries. According to Cem, one of the main obstacles is the lengthy process of registering new medications before they can enter the market. «We would like to bring our innovative products to these markets, but we need faster registration and approval procedures,» he explained. At the same time, Cem emphasized that Novo measures its performance by more than just commercial results. Because the Novo Nordisk Foundation controls the company, it places considerable emphasis on scientific research and addressing public health challenges. «Of course, we need to secure our financial results to continue research and development. But we are also looking at how we can make a difference in public health. That’s why we say, ‘Lasting health starts now.’ We need to act now. This is a major public health challenge, and we need to tackle it together,» he stressed. In particular, the company seeks to build close relationships with national healthcare systems, hoping that such cooperation will help develop effective disease prevention programs and accelerate the introduction of new medications to local markets. In Kazakhstan, where Novo has a fully established representative office, the company focuses on collaborating with local healthcare professionals. The company also organizes various events aimed at preventing and treating chronic diseases such as diabetes and obesity. Addressing the affordability of obesity medications, Cem said these treatments could become more accessible in the future. He explained that developing new drugs requires substantial investment in research and clinical trials. As a result, patents protect original medications for a certain period, allowing pharmaceutical companies to generate the revenue needed to finance further research and development. However, once patent protection expires, more affordable alternatives may enter the market. Cem pointed to the diabetes treatment market as an example, noting that it now includes numerous manufacturers and a wide range of medications. Meanwhile, the number of people living with overweight or obesity who may also need medical treatment is significantly larger than the number of people with diabetes. «In five to 10 years, many new products will be on the market. There will be more treatment options, and as patents expire, more affordable medications will become available,» he predicted. Given that obesity is often accompanied by other health conditions whose treatment places a substantial burden on public healthcare systems, the emergence of proven and affordable weight-management medications could represent a significant step forward, Cem concluded.

articles.title: Angela Rayner grants planning approval for asylum centre in Piddington despite local opposition
articles.summary: Home Office sign-off also needed for site that would house 1,200 asylum seekers near Oxfordshire village that voted to leave UK The communities secretary, Angela Rayner, has approved full planning permission for an asylum centre at a Ministry of Defence site near the village of Piddington in Oxfordshire. The decision approves plans to go ahead with the refurbishment and redevelopment of the former barracks.
articles.body: The communities secretary, Angela Rayner , has approved full planning permission for an asylum centre at a Ministry of Defence site near the village of Piddington in Oxfordshire. The decision approves plans to go ahead with the refurbishment and redevelopment of the former barracks. The Home Office insists that final approval is still to be determined. In September, people in Piddington voted to leave the UK in a symbolic referendum against plans to house 1,256 detained asylum seekers nearby. A total of 285 people were in favour of independence from the UK while 26 voted against. The poll was organised by campaigners for residents to demonstrate opposition to the plans for accommodation at the converted MoD site near the town of Bicester. A Home Office spokesperson said on Thursday: “Planning permission allows us to continue to progress the use of MoD Bicester. However, a final decision to proceed is yet to be taken. “The government is working on a fairer distribution of asylum accommodation across the country, with over £1bn saved in costs since the election. “This includes closing all asylum hotels and moving to alternative accommodation, including former military sites. These are designed to be self-contained, with 24/7 security and CCTV, to minimise the impact on the local community.” There is now a six-week window when the decision can face a legal challenge. A Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government spokesperson said: “The secretary of state has granted full planning permission for the temporary, phased use of the former MoD Bicester storage site. “As the decision may be subject to legal challenge, it would not be appropriate to comment further.” Last month, campaigners against the government plans took their complaints to the high court. The group Wrong Plan Wrong Site had appealed for a judicial review into the Home Office proposals for the former MoD Bicester site. In August, the government concluded an environmental assessment was unnecessary for the proposed development. But campaigners challenged that decision, with the group saying there were “credible concerns about potential significant environmental effects”. Last summer Andy Burnham said that people in more affluent areas of the UK must “play their part” in housing asylum seekers. Katie Lam, the shadow housing secretary of state, said: “Angela Rayner has told the people of Piddington that their voices count for nothing. “A village of a few hundred people will now have 1,256 illegal male migrants housed on its doorstep against the wishes of almost everyone who lives there. “Andy Burnham says every community must ‘play their part’ when it comes to housing illegal migrants, but why should British people suffer as a result of this government’s refusal to secure our border? The answer is not moving illegal migrants from hotels to military bases. It is removing them as soon as they arrive. The Home Office announced in June it was exploring the use of three former military sites to house asylum seekers: MoD Bicester, MoD Barnham and MoD Linton-on-Ouse. The government is also seeking to extend the use of two existing sites, Crowborough until 2030 and Wethersfield beyond 2027.

EU welcomes Abu Dhabi talks while preparing 22nd package of sanctions against Russia — EC
articles.summary: According to EC President Ursula von der Leyen, the EU would support Ukraine "be it in wartime or be it in peacetime"
articles.body: LONDON, November 12. /TASS/. The European Union welcomes the talks in Abu Dhabi while simultaneously preparing its 22nd package of sanctions against Russia, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said upon arriving in Dublin for the European Political Community summit. "I very much welcome the peace talks in Abu Dhabi," von der Leyen said, adding that the EU would support Ukraine "be it in wartime or be it in peacetime." Von der Leyen also said that, allegedly, European countries "were represented." At the same time, she emphasized that the EU was "preparing the 22nd sanctions package [against Russia]," as well as "a proposal on how to cover the financial needs of Ukraine in 2027," which it intends to present "before the next European Council," scheduled for November 26-27 in Brussels. Russia, the United States and Ukraine held talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11. The first round of consultations lasted four and a half hours, including a 40-minute break, on November 10, followed by a session that lasted about two hours on November 11. Presidential Aide Vladimir Medinsky led the Russian delegation, while Foreign Intelligence Service chief Rustem Umerov headed the Ukrainian delegation. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, NATO’s Supreme Allied Commander Europe Alexus Grynkewich and UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, were also present at the negotiating table when the talks began. Despite statements from French officials, no Europeans attended the meeting. Medinsky revealed that, at the talks, Russia and Ukraine coordinated a major POW exchange, saying that its parameters will be made public soon. He also noted that the theme of the European security system was central to the Abu Dhabi meeting and that the sides found common ground on some aspects of it.
